# Protocol: the two Wiki traces we had not run, `wiki_2016u` and `wiki_2019u` (frozen 2026-10-24, before any download of them)

**Why.** The paper's Wiki panel (Figures 3, 4, 5) has three traces; we ran only `wiki_2019t` (1.9 GB). The other two are public on the authors' CMU directory (23 GB and 25 GB). Earlier sessions did not fetch them because the disk and the 128 GiB aggregate budget did not allow it. `/home` now has 32 GB free; the two files fit one at a time. SIEVEREPRODUCTION has results for both (`fig4.csv`: `wiki_2016u` 2,803.5 M requests / 37.2 M objects, `wiki_2019u` 2,655.6 M requests / 49.7 M objects), so each can be compared three ways: ours, theirs, the paper's dots.

**Inputs.** `https://ftp.pdl.cmu.edu/pub/datasets/twemcacheWorkload/cacheDatasets/wiki/wiki_2016u.oracleGeneral.zst` first, then `wiki_2019u.oracleGeneral.zst`, one at a time (disk). Identity: HEAD length, `zstd -t`, SHA-256 of the stored file and of the decompressed stream, exact record count and exact distinct-object count over records with nonzero size (`scripts/twitter_sampled_extension.py fetch`, the same code used for every other file). Each file is deleted after all its runs are complete and recorded in `docs/data_removed_20261020.md` (URL and SHA-256 stay; counters, identity records and tables stay).

**Runs.** The 11 policies of the earlier batches (FIFO, LRU, CLOCK, SIEVE, ARC, TwoQ, LIRS, LHD, Hyperbolic, TinyLFU snapshot, B-LRU) at 0.1% and 10% of the exact distinct objects, capacity passed explicitly (floor(exact x fraction), because the simulator's own working-set estimate is sampled on files over 1 GiB), `--ignore-obj-size 1`, cold start, seed 42 for the random policies, the controlled-seed build that every earlier batch used. CACHEUS is expected to be omitted by the memory gate (policy-specific estimate 0.5 GiB + 600 B x 37-50 M objects is above the 12 GiB soft budget); it will be tried only if the estimate is under the budget, and an omission is recorded, not hidden. Memory gates, retry rounds and policy-specific estimates are those of `docs/twitter_gated_extension_protocol.md` (amendment 1). Extra TinyLFU runs (descriptive, check 3): the pre-fix build (`build/paper-tinylfu`) and the pinned build at SIEVEREPRODUCTION's capacities (`cache_size` column of its `fig4.csv`: 37,218 / 3,721,819 for `wiki_2016u`, 49,619 / 4,961,998 for `wiki_2019u`), because `docs/tinylfu_dot_check_protocol.md` showed TinyLFU is sensitive to a few objects of capacity.

**Pre-declared checks (reported whatever they give).**
1. Our deterministic policies (all but LHD, TinyLFU and CACHEUS; Hyperbolic is included because its seed is fixed) agree with SIEVEREPRODUCTION's `fig4.csv` miss ratios (4 decimals) within 0.0005 on every cell. Their capacity comes from the sampled estimate and ours from the exact count, so a few cells may differ; exceptions are listed with their size.
2. Our SIEVE reduction from FIFO is within 0.0005 of the paper's dot of the same trace on both caches. Dot of each trace: the one SIEVEREPRODUCTION matched (`fig4/summary.md`: `wiki_2016u` is dot 1 and `wiki_2019u` dot 2 in both panels, `wiki_2019t` dot 3; the values are in `fig4_paper_values.csv`); and, independent of that matching, the distance of our SIEVE value to the nearest dot of the Wiki panel.
3. TinyLFU (descriptive): for each of the four cells per file, the distance of the pre-fix and of the pinned build to the paper's dot of that trace, at SIEVEREPRODUCTION's capacities and at ours.
4. Figure 5 Wiki (descriptive): the best algorithm of each trace among the 11 we run, next to SIEVEREPRODUCTION's `fig5_best.csv` and the paper's bar; a CACHEUS omission can change a winner only if CACHEUS is best on that trace in SIEVEREPRODUCTION's table, and that is stated per trace.

**Reporting.** With all three Wiki traces, Figures 4/5's Wiki panels in `scripts/build_paper_figures.py` gain two traces; the Figure 3 union is not affected (Twitter only). Nothing here has a hypothesis that could be falsified beyond the checks above; a miss on check 1 or 2 is reported and investigated as a separate, dated amendment.

## Amendment 1 (2026-10-24, resource gating only; no result had been seen for the jobs it affects)

On `wiki_2019u` (49.7 M objects) the old policy-specific estimate (TwoQ, LIRS, TinyLFU, B-LRU: 0.25 GiB + 150 B per object, so 7.7 GiB, plus the 4 GiB headroom) exceeded the 10.9 GiB the machine had available, and two jobs were omitted by the gate although measured use is far lower. The 22 completed `wiki_2016u` runs (37.2 M objects) measured peak RSS per policy of at most 1.84 GiB (B-LRU 53 B/object, LIRS 37, TwoQ 27, TinyLFU 25, LHD 24, ARC 20, FIFO/LRU/CLOCK/SIEVE 12, Hyperbolic 10). For the jobs still to run the estimate is set to 0.25 GiB + 60 B per object for TwoQ, LIRS, TinyLFU and B-LRU and 0.25 GiB + 30 B per object for the others (`TWITTER_EXT_MEASURED_ESTIMATE=1`); CACHEUS keeps 0.5 GiB + 600 B per object (no measurement exists at this size). The live 12 GiB RSS guard is unchanged, so an underestimate is caught while the run is in progress and recorded as an omission. The estimate decides only whether a run is attempted; it does not enter the counters.

## Outcome (2026-10-25; `python3 -B scripts/wiki_full_compare.py compare`; 22 of 24 runs per file, CACHEUS omitted by the memory gate on both)

Identity (scripts/twitter_sampled_extension.py fetch): `wiki_2016u` 2,803,498,585 requests, 37,197,832 distinct objects; `wiki_2019u` 2,655,612,611 requests, 49,707,463 distinct objects; both equal SIEVEREPRODUCTION's counts (2,803.5 M / 37.2 M and 2,655.6 M / 49.7 M). Exact capacities 37,197 / 3,719,783 and 49,707 / 4,970,746 objects.

1. **Check 1: 32 of 32 deterministic cells agree with SIEVEREPRODUCTION within 0.0005** (16 per file; LHD, CACHEUS, TinyLFU excluded by the rule). No exceptions, although their capacities (37,218 / 3,721,819 and 49,619 / 4,961,998) come from the sampled estimate and differ from ours by 0.05-0.2%.
2. **Check 2: our SIEVE reduction is within 0.0003 of the paper's dot on all four cells** (2016u 0.0002 and 0.0002, 2019u 0.0000 and 0.0003; the nearest-dot distances are the same, so it does not depend on the dot matching).
3. **Check 3 (TinyLFU, descriptive).** Reduction against SIEVEREPRODUCTION's FIFO miss ratio, distance to the paper's dot:

| trace, cache | pinned at simulator's capacity | pre-fix at simulator's capacity | pre-fix at our exact capacity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2016u, 0.1% | 0.0021 | **0.0001** | 0.0000 |
| 2016u, 10% | 0.0028 | **0.0004** | 0.0008 |
| 2019u, 0.1% | 0.0019 | **0.0001** | 0.0039 |
| 2019u, 10% | 0.0027 | **0.0003** | 0.0006 |

At the simulator's capacities the pre-fix build is within 0.0004 of the paper's dot on all four cells and the pinned build 0.002-0.003 away, as on Meta CDN and Wiki 2019t (`docs/tinylfu_dot_check_protocol.md`). At our exact capacity the pre-fix result for `wiki_2019u` at 0.1% moves from 0.1499 to 0.1537 (49,619 vs 49,707 objects), the capacity sensitivity measured on Meta KV.
4. **Check 4 (best algorithm of those run, descriptive).** 3 of 4 cells agree with SIEVEREPRODUCTION's and the paper's winner: 2016u small SIEVE, 2016u large TinyLFU, 2019u large SIEVE. **2019u small differs: ours TinyLFU (0.1535), theirs and the paper's LHD.** Our LHD equals the paper's dot (0.1505); the difference is TinyLFU: the pinned build at our capacity gives 0.1535 and the pre-fix build at the simulator's 0.1499 (below LHD, so LHD wins). The cell is decided by the TinyLFU build and its capacity sensitivity (0.004), not by a policy difference. CACHEUS was not run on either trace; in SIEVEREPRODUCTION's table it is not the best on any of the four cells, so its omission does not change a winner.

**Not done here and why.** Figure 5's Wiki bar counts a fixed five-contender set (SIEVE, ARC, CLOCK, LRU, LFU) from six-policy counters; we did not run LFU on these two files and both files are deleted (`docs/data_removed_20261020.md`), so Figure 5's Wiki bar still counts `wiki_2019t` only. Figure 4's Wiki panel now has all three traces.

Files: `local_results/wiki_2016u_extension/`, `local_results/wiki_2019u_extension/` (counters, identity, omissions, `tinylfu_builds.csv`), `local_results/wiki_full_comparison.csv`, `local_results/wiki_full_tinylfu_builds.csv`.

## Amendment 2 (2026-10-25, before any CACHEUS run on the Wiki files): the four omitted CACHEUS cells

Both Wiki files were deleted after their runs (`docs/data_removed_20261020.md`, third and fifth removals) with CACHEUS omitted by an estimate of 0.5 GiB + 600 B per object. Ten CACHEUS runs on Meta KV (`docs/metakv_split_protocol.md`, outcome of amendment 2) and four on the gated Twitter files (`docs/twitter_gated_extension_protocol.md`, outcome of amendments 2 and 2a) measured at most 151 B per object (0.77-2.45 GiB), so that estimate was several times too high. The four cells (2016u and 2019u at 0.1% and 10%) are therefore attempted: each file is downloaded again, one at a time, and its SHA-256 must equal the recorded one before any run; CACHEUS only (`TWITTER_EXT_ONLY_POLICIES=cacheus`), seed 42, exact capacities as in the other runs, one run at a time, estimate 0.5 GiB + 100 B x objects (`TWITTER_EXT_CACHEUS_PER_OBJECT=100`: below the 151 B measured on Meta KV, so the live guard of 12 GiB process-tree RSS and 4 GiB available RAM is what protects the machine). A run the guard stops, or the pre-run gate omits, is recorded as an omission; it is not retried with a changed allowance. Each file is deleted again afterwards with a removal record. Check (descriptive, CACHEUS is random so no threshold): our reduction next to SIEVEREPRODUCTION's default draw and the paper's dot of the trace.

## Outcome of amendment 2 (2026-10-30): `wiki_2016u` CACHEUS completed; `wiki_2019u` CACHEUS still not run

The script (scratchpad, not kept: its log was lost with the temporary directory in a reboot on 2026-10-30; the run records below are in the repository) downloaded each file again, checked its SHA-256 against the recorded one and deleted it after its attempts. **`wiki_2016u`: both CACHEUS cells completed** with exact counters, none stopped by the guard: 0.1%: 1,407,603,915 misses of 2,803,498,585 requests (miss ratio 0.5021), peak RSS 2.77 GiB, 3,905 s; 10%: 210,171,197 misses (0.0750), peak RSS 3.80 GiB (about 110 B per object), 4,282 s. Reduction from FIFO 0.1330 at 0.1% and 0.3104 at 10%; SIEVEREPRODUCTION's default draw gives miss ratios 0.502 and 0.0749 (reductions 0.1331 and 0.3109 of its table) and the paper's dots of this trace are 0.1820 and 0.3109. So at 10% ours equals theirs and the paper's dot (distance 0.0005); at 0.1% ours equals theirs and both are 0.049 below the paper's dot, the cell SIEVEREPRODUCTION lists as its largest CACHEUS difference. CACHEUS is random and `docs/cacheus_seed_spread_protocol.md` found bimodal outcomes on Meta CDN; we ran one seed here, so we cannot say whether this gap is a draw or a real difference.

**`wiki_2019u` CACHEUS: omitted by the pre-run gate in all three rounds** (needs 9.13 GiB available at 100 B per object, the machine had 8.26-8.29 GiB; `local_results/wiki_2019u_extension/worker2/omitted.csv`). Nothing ran. The protocol forbids a changed allowance, and the file is deleted again. Re-running needs the 27.3 GB file (about 27 GB free disk; 13.5 GB are free now) and about 1 GiB more available RAM. With these two cells missing, Figure 4's Wiki panel has 11 of 12 algorithms on two traces and all but CACHEUS on `wiki_2019u`.
